title: Wrong options right on only one feature
statement: When an item tests combining features or sources, include a plausible wrong option right on only one, and key the item so only all of them together answer it.
example: One unit required its closest-case judgment to rest on at least 2 matching chart columns, with a wrong option matching only one.
detail: Archived lesson prompts for a Grade 3 reading course, built around a chart that gains a column each lesson, repeat the rule across units (`incept-package-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v2/authoring/prompts`, units 1, 5 and 6). Read-across lessons ask for checks that combine two columns, such as which trickster was clever and punished, rather than a single-cell lookup, and in the weather and water unit each wrong option mislabels one column while another is right. Cold-transfer lessons ask which taught case a new text most resembles, a judgment that must rest on at least two matching columns, with a wrong option that matches on only one, such as the same culture-region but the opposite motive.
against: The rule comes from archived authoring prompts, which record no results for these items. The source's own example admits the option is true and wrong only for what it leaves out: "true-sounding, but uses only the map and ignores that neither source states diet" (grade3-reading/artifacts/u4l2-build/GRADE5-AUDIT.md, lines 262-263); built that way it is a defensible answer, against one-answer-the-text-settles.
